sigwx.source: WAFS SIGWX (harmonised multi-timestep product, FL100–600) — NOAA/NWS Aviation Weather Center GeoJSON, https://aviationweather.gov/data/products/autosigwx/…
sigwx.label: OFFICIAL · WAFS SIGWX
sigwx.attribution: Official WAFS SIGWX forecast (FL100–600), issued by the World Area Forecast System (ICAO WAFS), data published by NOAA/NWS Aviation Weather Center (aviationweather.gov). Rendering by the LSY WX Relay; not an official NWS product.
sigwx.disclaimer: For situational awareness only — not for flight planning or operational use. Crews and dispatch use the official WAFC charts and SIGMETs.
sigwx.issuerNote: The files name no issuing centre (no KKCI/EGRR field); both World Area Forecast Centres generate this product from the same blended grids. Do not print KKCI or EGRR or "issued by WAFC Washington/London" next to it.
sigwx.licence: If made by WAFC Washington: US government work, "may be used without charge for any lawful purpose" (https://www.weather.gov/disclaimer); the originator is not stated in the files. No NOAA/NWS endorsement implied; no KKCI/EGRR codes or NOAA/NWS logos on our rendering.

product.usable: a fixed-time chart is usable ±3 h around its valid time (WAFC guide)

sigwx.choice: past days: one chart valid 12Z, from the 06Z run +6 h (the shortest lead, so the closest to what happened, and the chart current at 12Z); stand-ins 00Z +12 h, previous 18Z +18 h, previous 12Z +24 h. Week ahead: newest published run, its 12Z charts within T+6…T+48.
sigwx.format: features[]: { kind JET|TROP|CAT|ICE|CB|VA|TC|RAD, base, top (FL; null = not given — props.xxx = "XXX" in the source = below the FL100 floor), fl?, kt?, geom {type line|polygon|point, coords [[lat, lon], …] rounded to 0.1°; polygon rings open}, props {in: map areas touched, sev MOD|SEV, cov ISOL|OCNL|FRQ, name, pts (jets: [[lat, lon, kt, FL], …] speed points), whole (jet fl/kt describe the whole jet)} }. CAT = WAFS "turbulence" (clear-air, in-cloud and mountain-wave). JET base/top = lowest/highest core FL along the jet (not its depth). TROP fl = tropopause contour height. Clipped to the box of the areas touched, Douglas–Peucker 0.1°.

scoring.formula: turbulence MOD + 3 × SEV + 0.5 × (icing MOD + 3 × SEV) + CB area (FRQ × 2)
scoring.note: research proposal, a method demonstration, not a validated hazard measure

aheadCover.note: Week ahead: official SIGWX from the 00Z run of Sat 10 Oct reaches T+48 (Mon 12 Oct 00Z); charts for Sat 10 Oct and Sun 11 Oct 12Z. Mon 12 Oct–Fri 16 Oct (days 3–7) are NOT covered: no official SIGWX beyond 48 h (use the model-derived layer, labelled as such).

sigwxModel.source: NOAA GFS 0.5° (NCEP): analyses (past week) and forecasts (week ahead)
sigwxModel.label: MODEL-DERIVED · NOT AN OFFICIAL SIGWX
sigwxModel.disclaimer: Model-derived significant-weather picture computed by the LSY WX Relay from NOAA GFS data. Not an official WAFS SIGWX chart, not issued or checked by a WAFC or any meteorological authority; not for flight planning or operational use. CAT potential is the Ellrod TI1 index, which in comparable studies catches about 55–60 % of turbulence reports while also flagging 15–30 % of smooth air (AUC about 0.70–0.77); it misses convective and mountain-wave turbulence and is not a turbulence grade. CB areas follow the NCEP WAFS CB recipe from GFS convective rain; jets come from the GFS max-wind level. Symbols after ICAO Annex 3 / WMO-No. 49 Vol. II.
sigwxModel.attribution: Derived by the LSY WX Relay from NOAA GFS data (NOAA/NCEP, public domain). Not a NOAA/NWS product; not endorsed by NOAA.
sigwxModel.layout: per frame: grid points lat0 + j*res, lon0 + i*res, row-major south→north, west→east; each point summarises the GFS 0.5° points within ±1° (25 points)

encoding.trop: base64, one byte per point, FL = v*5, 0 = missing
encoding.cbExtent: rle of CB cover in tenths 0–8 (the 5th-highest of the 25 points)
encoding.cbTopFL: base64 FL/5 of the highest CB top in the cell, 0 = none
encoding.jets: path [[lat, lon, kt], …] in flow order (arrow at the end), 0.1°

cat.index: Ellrod & Knapp TI1 = vertical wind shear × total deformation, per 50-hPa layer, smoothed once (1-2-1); band = the higher of its two layers
cat.cell: class c when at least 5 of the 25 0.5° points reach its threshold
cat.option: calibration "percentile" (config.json sigwxModel.catCalibration or --cat-calibration percentile): class thresholds = 95th / 98th percentile of the cell values of each band and frame over all days with CAT in this snapshot, i.e. the top 5 % / 2 %

cb.method: NCEP UPP CLDRAD.f WAFS CB: cover = f(ln convective precipitation rate), capped at 0.8; kept where the convective cloud top is above 400 hPa and the cloud deeper than 300 hPa; top FL = pressure altitude of the cloud top
cb.time: past days: 6-h forecast of the 06Z cycle (rain averaged 06–12Z); ahead: the 12Z step (rain averaged over the 6 h before)

jets.method: axes through the speed maxima of the GFS max-wind level, ≥ 80 kt, ≥ 900 km; FL and kt at the maximum of each piece inside the frame; strongest 8 per frame and day
jets.depth: [base, top] FL of the 80-kt wind below and above the core (ICAO), only for cores ≥ 120 kt, from u/v at 500–100 hPa; null = beyond FL180 / FL530 or no depth shown
jets.limitation: one max-wind level per GFS column: a polar and a subtropical jet above the same point merge

trop.method: GFS ICAHT at the tropopause (pressure altitude) as FL, median of the cell

ahead.mode: latest complete cycle at run time

notes: CAT, CB: up to +72 h only; beyond that the week-ahead days carry jets and tropopause only.

gefscat.source: NOAA GEFS v12 0.5° (NCEP global ensemble: control + 30 perturbed members), forecasts
gefscat.label: MODEL-DERIVED · GEFS ENSEMBLE · NOT AN OFFICIAL SIGWX
gefscat.disclaimer: Model-derived ensemble probability computed by the LSY WX Relay from NOAA GEFS data. Not an official WAFS SIGWX chart or turbulence forecast, not issued or checked by a WAFC or any meteorological authority; not for flight planning or operational use. Each value is the share of the 31 GEFS members whose Ellrod TI1 index reaches the "CAT potential" threshold used by the model-derived SIGWX layer; it is the probability of a model index, not of turbulence, and not a turbulence grade. The index catches about 55–60 % of turbulence reports while also flagging 15–30 % of smooth air in comparable studies; it misses convective and mountain-wave turbulence. Days 4–7 are low confidence.
gefscat.attribution: Derived by the LSY WX Relay from NOAA GEFS data (NOAA/NCEP, public domain). Not a NOAA/NWS product; not endorsed by NOAA.

licence.name: Public domain (NOAA/NWS data)

gefscat.runChoice: latest 00Z at least 6 h old; else the 18Z before it; else the 00Z a day earlier
gefscat.layout: per area: grid points lat0 + j*res, lon0 + i*res, row-major south→north, west→east (the points of the model SIGWX and jet grids); byte = % of members (0–100), 255 = missing; each point summarises the GEFS 0.5° points within ±1° (25 points)

200.layers: 250–200 hPa (≈ FL340–390); the deterministic layer adds 200–150 hPa

250.layers: 300–250 and 250–200 hPa (≈ FL300–390), as the deterministic layer

cat.index: Ellrod & Knapp TI1 = vertical wind shear × total deformation, per 50-hPa layer (300–250, 250–200 hPa), smoothed once (1-2-1)
cat.member: a member flags a cell when at least 5 of its 25 0.5° points reach the threshold (the deterministic cell rule)
cat.value: percent of the members read that flag the cell
cat.heights: ensemble-mean (geavg) geopotential heights for the layer depth; each member's own winds
cat.wording: "x % of members"; never a moderate/severe grade

check.what: control member: CAT flags with its own heights vs the ensemble-mean heights all members use (cells × bands × areas)

notes: Days 4–7 are low confidence; the FL300 and FL390 bands use one 50-hPa layer each (the GEFS 0.5° file has no 350 / 150 hPa), so they can read lower than the deterministic layer would.
